name: Éowyn, Shieldmaiden
oracle_text:
First strike
At the beginning of combat on your turn, if another Human entered the battlefield under your control this turn, create two 2/2 red Human Knight creature tokens with trample and haste. Then if you control six or more Humans, draw a card.
blocked_sentences: At the beginning of combat on your turn, if another Human entered the battlefield under your control this turn, create two 2/2 red Human Knight creature tokens with trample and haste. Then if you control six or more Humans, draw a card.

needs.what: A per-turn ledger tally of permanents that have *entered the battlefield* this turn, filterable by a selector rather than only by player -- suggested `{"permanents_entered_this_turn": {"controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Human"], "exclude_self": true}}`, read with an ordinary `cmp` against `{"const": 1}` the way morbid reads `creatures_died_this_turn`. It must record enough about each entering object to answer the selector *after that object has left* (a Human that entered and then died this turn still satisfies the printed condition), so the natural implementation is to append a snapshot of derived characteristics plus controller-at-entry to `TurnLedger` inside `GameState.emit` for `EventType.PERMANENT_ENTERS`, and clear it at cleanup with the rest of the ledger. `exclude_self` on the selector is what makes "*another* Human" sayable -- Éowyn is herself a Human, and she may well have entered this turn, which is exactly the case the word "another" exists to exclude.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `TurnLedger` (`src/automtg/engine/structs.py:206-286`) has seven tallies -- `creatures_died`, `attacked`, `damage_taken`, `life_lost`, `spells_cast`, `cards_to_graveyard`, `combat_damage_types` -- and entering the battlefield is not among them; `VALUE_KEYS` (`engine/effects/values.py:30-109`) exposes exactly those, so there is no `permanents_entered_this_turn` to ask for. Nothing in `src/` matches /entered.*this_turn/ outside a test name. The closest condition leaf is `exists`, which is a *board* query: `{"exists": {"controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Human"], "zone": "battlefield", "exclude_self": true}}` asks "do you control another Human", which is a strictly different and much weaker question -- it is true when a Human has sat there since turn three and nothing entered, and false when a Human entered this turn and died, so it gets the card wrong in both directions. The other candidate is `set_flag`/`has_flag`, and it fails on two counts. It has the wrong lifetime: `op_set_flag` (`engine/effects/ops_board.py:1049-1053`) does `obj.flags.add(flag)` and flags are cleared only by `reset_permanent_state` on a zone change (`engine/objects.py:426`), never at cleanup, so a flag set the first time a Human entered would leave the intervening-if permanently satisfied for the rest of the game -- the ability would fire every combat forever. And it has the wrong shape: writing the flag needs a second `permanent_enters` triggered ability that no printed line asks for, which the residual gate would reject, since every ability's `text` must be a printed sentence. `combat_damage_by` shows the intended precedent for a characteristic-keyed ledger read (prowl matches on creature subtype), but it only watches combat damage to a player and cannot be pointed at enters-the-battlefield.

closest_existing: token_pool / human_knight_2_2_r_trample_haste (already requested by forth_eorlingas and oath_of_eorl)
rest_is_expressible: First strike is already done by the free tier (`keywords: ["first_strike"]`) and needs nothing. The one triggered line is a single printed sentence, so its blocked intervening-if blocks the whole line and no partial answer was written -- writing the trigger without the "entered this turn" gate would make Éowyn fire every single combat unconditionally, which is a strictly stronger card, and the residual gate would have no way to see the missing clause because the `text` would still quote the printed line in full. Everything else on that line already loads: "At the beginning of combat on your turn" is `{"event": "begin_combat", "controller": "you"}` (the shape `auto/templates.cards.json:40174-40184` uses for a Lieutenant trigger, with the intervening-if as the trigger's `condition`); "create two ... tokens" is `{"op": "create_token", "token": "human_knight_2_2_r_trample_haste", "amount": {"const": 2}}` once the token exists; and "Then if you control six or more Humans, draw a card" is a plain `{"op": "if", "condition": {"cmp": {"left": {"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Human"]}}, "op": ">=", "right": {"const": 6}}}, "then": [{"op": "draw", "player": "you", "amount": {"const": 1}}]}` -- note it must stay an `if` *inside* the effects rather than a second trigger condition, because "Then" is evaluated after the tokens are created and counts them. For whoever closes this: the sandbox can still observe the card even fully unblocked, but only weakly. The harness casts Éowyn in the precombat main phase and stops, so the begin-combat trigger never fires and the intervening-if would be false anyway (Éowyn herself does not count, and no other Human enters), which makes the honest expectation `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33}` -- trap 5 in the brief. Verifying the trigger properly needs a second Human entering earlier in the turn and combat actually being reached, which this fixed position does not provide.
